note: [agent-bulk] shw 17010 (174.8 MeV, 5 seg, len 34.7) is complete: members run 0-64.6 cm at 0-22.6 deg from one X, every non-member within 60 cm is at 48-175 deg, and the only non-member below 40 deg at ANY distance is 47017 (3.3 MeV) at 85.0 cm / 24.5 deg. Nothing contiguous is missing and the set does not span two directions. Shape caveat, in the pilot's evt284791 sense: the seed is a NARROW ~20-25 cm chain (point cloud about +-0.8 cm in both az -55 and az +85) followed by four small detached blobs at 24.0, 43.7, 50.9 and 64.6 cm - sparse, and I did not test whether those far blobs belong. I make NO PID claim here; correct means nothing is missing. THE USEFUL NEGATIVE - why this event has no pi0 and should not have one: the display's pi0 probe pairs 17010 with 11009 (58.6 MeV) and the VERTEX convention gives theta 93.5 deg -> m = 147.3 MeV, which is inside the code's accept window and would look like a good pi0 on the numbers alone. It is not one. Reading the segment owners, 11009 sits at the far END of the ~90 cm track that leaves the nu vertex - segments 11004 (pdg 211) and 11008 (pdg 13), both unowned grey, running star -> blob in all three vertex frames. So 11009 is a decay product at the end of a charged track (Michel-like), not a converted photon, and the reconstruction was RIGHT to accept no pi0 group. This is a case where the mass number and the topology disagree and the topology wins. Not looked at: the other 10 showers, all at or below 4.0 MeV (scope rule min_kine_best 20 MeV); I did not judge 11009's own completeness.
